_comment: ADR-Bench evaluation checklist for Arena Hub fleet connectors. Source of facts: uber/ADR Detection/README.md and top-level README. ADR-Bench: 304 scenarios (261 benign, 43 malicious), 134 MCP servers, coverage of 17 agent attack techniques. The full 17-technique enumeration is in the ADR MLSys 2026 paper (docs/adr-paper.pdf in uber/ADR); only categories directly documented in the repo README files are named below — do not treat this list as the complete 17.

documented_categories.evidence: Detection/README: 'location_harvester' registered under spoofed community identity 'weather_forecast_service' as a supply-chain-impersonation test case
Detection/README: AgentDojo integration for prompt-injection evaluation; ADR-Bench includes 43 malicious tasks
Detection/README: 26 vulnerable MCP servers with embedded vulnerabilities for discovery (EAS target tools)

fleet_checklist: Run ADR Discovery against every fleet host to inventory AI apps, CLI agents, IDE extensions, model runtimes, MCP servers; flag unknown surfaces
Wire each connector's session logs through extensions/connector-security/src/schema.ts into ADR AgentEvent shape
Replay the 43 ADR-Bench malicious scenarios against each connector in an isolated environment before fleet admission
Confirm detector two-tier behavior: high-recall triage flags suspicious sessions, deeper reasoning confirms — tune for fleet false-positive rate
Re-check on every connector change (new model, new MCP server, new wake path)
